faq_heading: Trunk or Treat Sign-Up Sheet FAQ

plan.angle: The top 10 for trunk or treat sign up sheet is printables and editable Etsy, Canva and Pinterest sheets: one grid of blanks for name, car and theme. None of them can stop two families claiming the same theme, remind volunteers, or tell trunk hosts how much candy to bring once the RSVPs are in. This page shows the sign-up sheet as a small app for four real jobs: a church assigning parking spots and themes, a PTO filling volunteer shifts, a fire company sizing candy from family RSVPs, and a car dealership running a best trunk vote. The FAQ covers how many trunks to plan, what to ask families, allergy-friendly trunks, timing and weather changes.
tab_stories: At Ridgefold Community Church, Noreen Vasquerra opens 30 trunk spots; 26 are claimed, and when the Tillery family picks Under the Sea, which the Prudhomme family already holds at spot 9, the sheet asks them for another theme.

The Brookhaw Elementary PTO splits the night into setup, candy table and cleanup shifts with 14 slots; 12 are filled, cleanup still needs 2 people, and every volunteer gets an email reminder the day before.
At Mabrey Volunteer Fire Company, 87 families RSVP with 212 kids, so coordinator Gwen Ilsley's sheet emails each of the 18 trunk hosts to bring at least 212 pieces of candy.

Durrance Motors runs a best trunk vote on its lot; families cast 148 votes before voting closes at 7:30 pm, and Haunted Barn wins with 41 votes, which sales manager Cosmo Lunetti sees on the results page.
